A company acting on behalf of the Israeli government signed a contract last
month with an American company that advertises its access to a database of
more than 25 million "verified conservatives" to help Israel influence U.S.
public opinion, according to newly disclosed federal documents.

Starboard LLC, headed by American media executive Ryan Coyne, signed an
agreement with an Israeli influencer marketing firm acting "on behalf of the
State of Israel," according to the documents, which were recently disclosed in
line with the Foreign Agents Registration Act, or FARA.

The contract comes as the Israeli government contends with increasing
hostility from sections of the Republican base over Israel's role in drawing
the U.S. into a wildly unpopular war in Iran. Starboard is an important
partner for any effort to influence conservatives in the U.S. The company
acquired the right-wing social media site Parler in 2023, and quickly sold it
later that year. But even after the sale of Parler, Starboard kept "data used
for email and text message marketing," Coyne told WIRED in a March 2024
[interview](https://www.wired.com/story/parler-app-store-free-speech-
censorship/).

Starboard also owns or promotes several conservative news websites, including
American Wire and BizPac Review. Its most popular website is PolitiBrawl, a
publisher of political content that attracts substantial audiences on media
platforms like YouTube and Facebook. Its[ Substack
account](https://substack.com/@politibrawl) lists more than 1.3 million
subscribers.

The $500,000 contract, dated October 13 and filed with the Justice Department
on October 28, outlines a 120-day campaign of public influence on behalf of
Israel. The contract establishes a "persuasion pilot program that measures
contact impact and sentiment analysis through regular polling," followed by
"continuous content deployment, optimization, and measurement" to assess user
sentiment. The contract requires Starboard to produce a final report that
assesses the cost of changing a user's opinion, a metric referred to in the
contract to as "Cost-Per-Converted-Voice."

Starboard continues to advertise its access to the data of conservative
social-media users through its prior ownership of the platform and a broader
network of conservative media platforms.

On its website, Starboard states that its acquisition of Parler gives the
company and its clients access to the platform's politically engaged user
base. Starboard and Parler did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

Starboard has previously performed fundraising work for President Donald
Trump, and its website lists past work with Turning Point USA and conservative
political figures like Matt Gaetz, Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), Rep. Elise
Stefanik (R-N.Y.), and Vivek Ramaswamy. Starboard's website also advertises
services in strategic communications and government relations, boasting that
it "provides unparalleled expertise in navigating U.S. policy, regulations,
and global opportunities, particularly now under the Trump administration."

## Parler Games

Parler was founded during Trump's first term as a self-styled free-speech
alternative to mainstream social-media platforms, attracting a range of
conservatives and far-right activists who accused platforms like Twitter and
Facebook of censoring their views.

The platform became a focus of national controversy after the January 6, 2021,
attack on the U.S. Capitol. Among the rioters that day were Parler users, some
of whom were arrested. The social-media company's "unique business model and
content moderation policies were likely a contributing factor in fomenting
some of the violence" during the attack, according to
[research](https://www.newamerica.org/insights/parler-and-the-road-to-the-
capitol-attack/executive-summary/) published by the public-policy think tank
New America. Days later, Apple and Google removed Parler from their app
stores, and Amazon suspended its web-hosting services over concerns about the
platform's failure to moderate its content.

In April 2023, Starboard, previously known as Olympic Media, purchased Parler
for an undisclosed sum. At the time, Coyne was
[explicit](https://halifax.citynews.ca/2023/04/14/digital-conglomerate-buys-
right-wing-app-parler/) about the value of owning access to Parler's
conservative user base, describing it as an opportunity to expand Starboard's
advertising and publishing businesses. He said his company looked forward to
"integrating that audience across all of our existing platforms."

Later that year, Starboard
[sold](https://apnews.com/article/24033455bdbadb3c07322bb3129feddb) the
platform to PDS Partners, whose owners included former Republican political
operative Ryan Rhodes, who became Parler's CEO, and Elise Pierotti, a former
Parler marketing executive who returned as its chief marketing officer. The
identities of other investors were not publicly disclosed. PDS Partners is
structured as a limited liability company. Rhodes and Pierotti have described
themselves as its partial owners, while declining to identify remaining
investors, leaving Parler's full ownership and financing structure unclear.

The Israeli government's hiring of Starboard comes amid a major spending
campaign to shore up American support for Israel among conservatives who have
increasingly [soured](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-
reads/2026/04/07/negative-views-of-israel-netanyahu-continue-to-rise-among-
americans-especially-young-people/) on the U.S. relationship with the country
--particularly younger generations angered by the war in Iran and U.S. support
for Israel. Israel's 2026 budget [allocated](https://www.jpost.com/israel-
news/article-894645) roughly $730 million to its global public-relations
budget, more than four times what it spent the previous year.

Israel has increased its interventions in U.S. public opinion over the last
year, according to Eli Clifton, cofounder of the Quincy Institute for
Responsible Statecraft. "This is in response to collapsing public support that
extends all the way into conservative and evangelical communities that have
long been seen as the electoral lynchpin for Israel's political support within
the U.S.," Clifton, co-author of the book "Israel's Lobby," told Drop Site
News.

"Retaining the support of conservatives and Republicans is vital if Israel
will continue to maintain the status-quo levels of support it currently
enjoys, despite the majority of Americans wanting greater distance between the
U.S. government and Israel's genocide in Gaza," he added.

In a speech to evangelical Christian leaders in Florida in [December
2025](https://www.timesofisrael.com/pm-tells-evangelical-leaders-israel-is-
part-of-effort-to-protect-christians-worldwide/), Israeli Prime Minister
Benjamin Netanyahu described the battle for public opinion in the United
States as the "eighth front" in Israel's wars. Ordinary Americans, "especially
on the conservative wing of the United States," must be a major focus of
Israeli influence campaigns, he added.

Israel's public-relations spending spree has targeted both political
conservatives and younger evangelicals across the country, using online
platforms, right-wing media outlets, Christian influencers, and even location-
based ad [campaigns](https://responsiblestatecraft.org/israel-geofencing-
churches/) targeting places of worship. In July, an Israeli Foreign Ministry
official [told](https://time.com/article/2026/07/13/brad-parscale-israel-
influence-operation/) TIME magazine that a central objective of the
government's influence campaigns in the U.S. was to prevent conservatives from
turning against Israel. The official added that the country was looking for
partners "who understood the landscape of the internet and MAGA culture."

## "Cost-Per-Converted-Voice"

The contract was signed by Coyne, and lists an executive of the Israeli firm
working on the state's behalf, Udi Mendelovits, chief financial officer of
LDRS Group, or Leaders.

The FARA documents do not provide many details about the pilot program, but
they indicate that Starboard is expected to identify target audiences and
develop measurements of users' political views. The aims of the contract
include "Audience Development and Panel Construction," "Content Production and
Distribution," and "Optimization and Analytics," to be performed by Starboard
over the course of the engagement.

According to the filing, Starboard is also required to measure how much it
costs to change an individual's views--what the contract calls a "Cost-Per-
Converted-Voice" assessment.

The contracting intermediary, [Leaders](https://ldrsgroup.com/about/), has
previously organized social-media campaigns on behalf of the Israeli
government. In February 2024, the company
[contracted](https://efile.fara.gov/docs/7662-Exhibit-AB-20251012-3.pdf) Davis
Media NY to manage up to ten influencers producing pro-Israel content for
social media. In December 2023, representatives of Leaders approached
influencers in the U.S. and offered to pay them to promote content on
Instagram, the Washington Post
[reported](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2024/01/24/gaza-israel-
activism-online/). FARA documents filed as recently as 2025
[identified](https://efile.fara.gov/docs/7662-Exhibit-AB-20251012-3.pdf)
Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs as the government agency represented
through Leaders.

Although the formal agreement in the new filing names Leaders as Starboard's
client, the[ ](https://efile.fara.gov/docs/7788-Exhibit-
AB-20261028-1.pdf)document footnotes repeatedly identify the agreement as
"Starboard x Havas Frankfurt,"**** an apparent reference to Havas Media
Germany, the Frankfurt-based subsidiary of the French advertising giant Havas.
Leaders, Havas and the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not respond to
request for comment.

Havas has served as a major intermediary for Israeli government-funded
communications campaigns in the United States, working on behalf of Israel's
Government Advertising Agency to hire American political consultants,
advertising agencies, and public-relations firms. Among its
[contractors](https://www.odwyerpr.com/story/public/23658/2025-09-29/trumps-
ex-digital-guru-works-combat-antisemitism.html) is [Clock Tower
X](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/israel-brad-parscale-ai-chatbots-gaza), a
firm headed by Trump's former campaign manager Brad Parscale. In 2025, Clock
Tower X agreed to a four-month contract with Havas for an initial $6 million.

That agreement called for the production of at least 100 original pieces of
pro-Israel content for social media each month, with 80% targeting Gen Z
audiences. The agreement also specified the integration of messaging into one
of the country's largest conservative Christian media companies, Salem Media
Network, in addition to efforts to shape how information about Israel appears
in search engines and in LLM responses.

Starboard explicitly advertises its ability to promote clients' content
through its YouTube audience and its online publications. Its marketing
materials also advertise services for its clients including email marketing,
text messaging, video advertising, and creative testing.

The contract signed with Leaders on behalf of the Israeli government does not
specify what channels, if any, Starboard would use to promote pro-Israel
messaging to conservative American social media users.
